title: Ram Setu: The Real Secret Behind the Legend
description:
Ram Setu (also called Adam’s Bridge) is often claimed to be a bridge built by Lord Ram’s vanara sena as told in the Ramayana. In this video we critically examine that claim through scientific evidence: geology, radiometric dating, remote sensing, historical surveys, and expert opinions.

We look at what the Geological Survey of India, CSIR, ASI and NIO have said. We show how satellite and bathymetric data indicate the structure is a natural chain of limestone shoals, sandbanks and coral reefs, formed over thousands of years due to changes in sea level during the Pleistocene and Holocene eras.

The ASI (Archaeological Survey of India) in 2007 declared there was no evidence that the formation is man-made.  Radiometric and thermoluminescence dating in proposed recent studies aim to test age claims, but so far they have not delivered proof of any human construction. 

We expose misuses of NASA images and exaggerated interpretations: for example, claims that images show stones placed by humans are contradicted by NASA and multiple geological experts who say the formation is natural. 

Sea-level data shows that about 7,000 years ago, parts of the Palk Strait were exposed land; subsequent submersion created the shallow water channels and reef systems we see today. There is no scientifically accepted evidence that the “bridge” was engineered by a vanara army or human effort.

If you’ve searched for Ram Setu myth vs science, Adam’s Bridge geology, ASI report Ram Setu, Ramayana literal or allegorical, or scientific dating Ram Setu, Ram Setu ICESat-2 study, Adam’s Bridge bathymetry 2024, archaeology vs geology Ram Setu, peer reviewed evidence Ram Setu, this video cuts through the hype and focuses on verifiable facts.

Like, comment, share, and help spread clarity over myth. Let’s hype the facts together.

**********************Latest Updates since the video was made*********************
A 2024 study using ICESat-2 satellite data produced a high-resolution digital bathymetric elevation model (DBEM) of Adam’s Bridge. It confirms that about 29 km of ridge extends submerged between Dhanushkodi (India) and Talaimannar (Sri Lanka). Nearly 99.98 percent of the structure’s volume lies underwater; only ~0.02 percent is exposed above sea level. (More exposed parts are just sandbanks, not solid rock or human stonework.) 

That study also found highly undulating topography under super-shallow water, sudden depth changes, and transverse slopes on either side of the ridge which are consistent with natural sediment deposition and erosion from sea currents rather than precise engineering. 

Another recent work, “Adam’s Bridge: Sacrality, Performance, and Heritage of an Oceanic Marvel” (2024) by Arup K. Chatterjee, treats the bridge more as a socio-cultural and geological marvel, recognizing its natural coralline ridges, patch reefs, and sand shoals as ecological heritage rather than evidence of construction. It emphasizes that many of the “mythic” claims do not stand up under interdisciplinary scrutiny. 

Furthermore, criticism has also arisen in studies of public narrative, law, and archaeology (e.g. Ram Setu and Delusions of Archaeological Grandeur, 2024), pointing out that many claims about human engineering are based more in popular belief, film, or selective history rather than scientifically verified data.

2 - Recent geological surveys show that the stones (they are limestone shoals - not pumice stone as you call it) are about 7000 years old, while the sand underneath is about 4000 years old. This indicates that the stones were deliberately placed here, brought from elsewhere. University of Southern Oregon, Indiana university and University of Colorado are some of the sources for this information.
